findings.ours: TGTabBar.m:117-176 - tap only commits on touchesEnded; touchesBegan sets a pending index and touchesMoved/touchesCancelled can revert to _touchStartIndex, so the delegate (and the actual tab switch) fires on lift.
findings.theirs: The tab switches on touch-down: touchesBegan sets the index and calls the delegate immediately; there is no touchesMoved/touchesEnded/touchesCancelled at all, so dragging off the bar cannot cancel a switch.
findings.fix: Delete -touchesMoved:, -touchesEnded:, -touchesCancelled: and the _tracking/_touchStartIndex/_pendingIndex ivars from TGTabBar.m; in -touchesBegan: compute index, [self setSelectedIndex:index] and call [self.tabDelegate tabBarSelectedItem:index] right there.

findings.ours: RootViewController.m:74-77 - tabBarSelectedItem: only acts when the index changes; tapping the already-selected tab does nothing.
findings.theirs: Tapping the selected tab again sends scrollToTopRequested to the selected view controller, scrolling the chat/contact list back to the top.
findings.fix: In RootViewController -tabBarSelectedItem: add an else branch: if ([self.selectedViewController respondsToSelector:@selector(scrollToTopRequested)]) [self.selectedViewController performSelector:@selector(scrollToTopRequested)]; and implement -scrollToTopRequested on the chat list / contacts / settings controllers (setContentOffset to -contentInset.top, animated).

findings.ours: RootViewController.m:69-72 - customTabBar.hidden is flipped when a child navigation controller pushes, so the bar disappears/reappears abruptly mid push animation.
findings.theirs: The tabs controller is the root of a single outer TGNavigationController; pushes happen on that outer stack, so the whole tabs view (bar included) slides off together. The tab bar is never hidden and never toggles.
findings.citation: TGAppDelegate.mm:303 ([TGNavigationController navigationControllerWithRootController:_mainTabsController]) plus the absence of any hidden= on _customTabBar in TGMainTabsController.m:353-365
findings.fix: Push detail controllers on the outer navigation controller (self.navigationController of RootViewController) instead of per-tab UINavigationControllers, and remove the -navigationController:willShowViewController: hidden toggle at RootViewController.m:69-72.

findings.ours: RootViewController.m:30-42 wraps each tab in its own UINavigationController, so each tab carries its own nav bar and title, and switching tabs cross-fades two different bars.
findings.theirs: One shared navigation bar owned by the outer navigation controller; the tabs controller pulls title / titleView / left+right bar button items from the child via TGTabControllerChild and updates them in place, with a 0.1s CATransition on the title when it changes, and honours navigationBarShouldBeHidden per child.
findings.fix: Adopt the original structure: children conform to a TGTabControllerChild-style protocol (controllerTitle, controllerTitleView:, controllerLeft/RightBarButtonItem, navigationBarShouldBeHidden) and RootViewController writes them onto its own navigationItem on selection, with the 0.1s kCAMediaTimingFunctionEaseIn CATransition on the title layer.

findings.ours: RootViewController.m:21-25 - the TGHacks layout delegate is installed on self.view only.
findings.theirs: It is installed on self.view AND on self.view.subviews[0] (the UITabBar content container), which is what forces the transition view to fill the container's bounds; without it child content can be laid out short by the tab-bar height.
findings.fix: In RootViewController -loadView also call [TGHacks setLayoutDelegateForContainerView:self.view.subviews[0] layoutDelegate:<a second TGTabsContainerViewDelegate instance>] (guarding for a non-empty subviews array), retaining it like self.layoutDelegate.

findings.ours: TGTabBar.m:97-115 - setSelectedIndex only calls setNeedsLayout, so the white selection PNG moves on the next layout pass rather than at the moment of the touch.
findings.theirs: setSelectedIndex recomputes indicatorWidth/paddingLeft and assigns _selectedView.frame synchronously inside the setter (duplicating the layoutSubviews math), so the highlight snaps under the finger immediately.
findings.fix: In TGTabBar -setSelectedIndex: compute indicatorWidth/paddingLeft/additionalWidth/additionalOffset and set self.selectedView.frame = CGRectMake(paddingLeft + indicatorWidth*_selectedIndex + additionalOffset, 0, indicatorWidth + additionalWidth, 49) directly, in addition to (or instead of) setNeedsLayout.

findings.ours: RootViewController.m:38-42 - the third tab is TGSettingsViewController, a settings list.
findings.theirs: The third tab (labelled Settings.TabTitle) is the user's own profile page, TGProfileController initWithUid:0, i.e. the account screen with avatar/phone/username at the top and settings below.
findings.citation: TGAppDelegate.mm:293 and 298 ([[TGProfileController alloc] initWithUid:0 ...] placed third in setViewControllers:)
findings.fix: Make the third tab open our profile/account screen (own avatar, name, phone header) with the settings rows below it, rather than a bare settings table; keep the tab caption "Settings".

findings.ours: RootViewController.m:93-113 - the tab badge sums unread only over unmuted chats and also writes applicationIconBadgeNumber.
findings.theirs: TGTabBar setUnreadCount: is fed a single count and renders it; no muting filter or app-icon badge is applied in the tabs controller.
findings.fix: Keep the arithmetic if the muted-chat concept is deliberate, but move it out of the tab controller; do not let the mute filter make the tab badge disagree with the chat list's own unread badges.
